title: Six Major Labs Sign the EU Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content
hook: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Mistral all put their names to Europe's code for marking AI-generated content — the practical layer under the AI Act's transparency rules.
key_points: Signatories reported: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Mistral — most of the frontier lab landscape in one document.
The code covers transparency of AI-generated content: marking and disclosing synthetic text, images, audio and video.
It sits under the EU AI Act's transparency obligations, giving providers a concrete way to show compliance.
Codes of practice in the EU are voluntary instruments — signing is a compliance route, not itself the law.
Commenters expect the commitments to reach these labs' open-weight releases, not just their hosted APIs.
content_html: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, Microsoft and Mistral have all signed the EU's Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content — effectively the whole frontier-lab field agreeing on one set of commitments about labelling synthetic media.
extra_html:
Why this matters

The EU AI Act sets transparency obligations for AI-generated content, but the regulation says what must happen, not how. Codes of practice fill that gap: they are voluntary instruments drawn up with industry, and signing one is a recognised way for a provider to show it is meeting the underlying legal duty. Getting six of the largest model providers onto the same code is the interesting part — it turns marking AI output from a per-company policy choice into something closer to an industry baseline.

The open question is technical rather than legal. Related cards in this deck cover research showing that current text-watermarking schemes are easy to strip with paraphrasing and produce high false-negative rates even unattacked. A transparency regime that leans on marking is only as strong as the marks, and that gap is where the next round of argument will happen.

Reported via r/LocalLLaMA; see the linked discussion, and the European Commission's AI Act pages for the authoritative text.

related.title: The EU AI Act
related.hook: The EU's answer to regulating AI: sort systems by how much risk they pose, then scale the rules to match — from outright bans to no rules at all.

related.title: AI Watermark Evidence Fails Forensic Readiness
related.hook: Laws like the EU AI Act and California's SB 942 assume watermark detection can hold up in court. Tested against forensic and legal admissibility standards, three leading methods collapse.

related.title: Linear Ensembles Wash Away Watermarks
related.hook: Text watermarks survive paraphrasing — but not arithmetic. Averaging the outputs of 3–5 different models cancels the signal almost entirely, and improves quality while doing it.

flashcards.prompt: What is the legal status of an EU code of practice like this one?

choices.text: Voluntary — signing is one route to demonstrating compliance
Binding legislation that replaces the AI Act's transparency articles
A court ruling that applies retroactively to past model releases

flashcards.explanation_html: Codes of practice are voluntary instruments. The AI Act sets the obligations; the code gives providers a concrete, agreed way to show they are meeting them.

flashcards.prompt: Why does this code matter for open-weight models and not just hosted APIs?
flashcards.back_html: The signing labs also ship open-weight releases. Transparency commitments about marking AI-generated content follow the content those models produce, wherever the weights end up running.

flashcards.prompt: What problem does existing research raise about relying on watermarks to satisfy such transparency rules?

choices.text: Watermarks are fragile — paraphrasing removes them at very high rates
Watermarks are impossible to embed in text at all
Watermarks only work on video, never on images

flashcards.explanation_html: Work on watermark forensics found simple paraphrase attacks stripped detection in nearly every run, so a policy layer built on marking has a shaky technical floor.
